sanskrit: smara smaro 'si devair datto 'si smara | amuṣya mana ā smara yathāhaṃ kāmaye tathā ||
english: Remember! You are Smara; you have been given by the gods — remember! Fix upon the mind of that man yonder; let it be just as I desire.

sanskrit: śocayāsya hṛdayaṃ kāma gaccha- -aṅgajvaro dahatu śocatu tmanā | saṅkalpā asya samarantādhībhir iyam evāsya digamahanyanyāḥ ||
english: Burn his heart; go, O Kāma! Let the fever in his limbs blaze and torment of itself. Let his longings be consumed by obsessive thoughts — this woman alone shall be his direction; no other day, no other.

sanskrit: nirānandāḥ pramucchado manomuho nayuvo naṣṭakṛtvā araṇyavaḥ | āveśinīḥ pradrupo ropayiṣṇur eta āstādhyaḥ pra hiṇomi brahmaṇā ||
english: Joyless, causing swoons, confounders of the mind, leading astray, making one lose his purpose, roaming the wilderness — those ādhyaḥ that enter and possess, that spread and inflame: these very obsessive thoughts I send forth with the sacred formula.

sanskrit: hṛtkartanī ṛtudā grāmānnāśanīḥ svapnacchida ughnanīghnā manomuhaḥ | āveśinīḥ pradrupo ropayiṣṇur eta āstādhyaḥ pra hiṇomi brahmaṇā ||
english: Lacerators of the heart, timely ones, destroyers of village-food, severers of sleep, killers of the mighty, confounders of the mind — those ādhyaḥ that enter and possess, that spread and inflame: these very obsessive thoughts I send forth with the sacred formula.

sanskrit: indrāgnī mitrāvaruṇā te adya- -ubhe ca dyāvāpṛthivī mātariśvā | aśvinā devaḥ savitā bhagaś ca manas ta u ghnantu na ramāsā atra ||
english: Indra and Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, both Heaven and Earth, Mātariśvan, the Aśvins, god Savitṛ, and Bhaga — let all of these smite his mind; let him find no repose here.

sanskrit: trayastriṃśat tvā uta ghnantu devā ādhyaś cittam upa te bharantām | bharadvājasya matayas ta īśatāṃ chinneva naur bandhanāt pra plavasva ||
english: Let the thirty-three gods smite you; let the ādhyaḥ carry obsessive thoughts right into you. Let the incantations of Bharadvāja have dominion over you — drift away like a boat cut loose from its mooring!

sanskrit: etāḥ patanty ādhyo vārṣikīr iva vidyutaḥ | tāsāṃ pratigraho bhava sāyaṃ goṣṭhe gavām iva ||
english: These ādhyaḥ fly down like lightning-flashes of the rainy season. Become the receiver of them at evening, as cows return to their pen.

sanskrit: ni śīrṣato ni pātita ādhyo veśayāmi te | tās tvā samuttudantīr bodhayantīr upāsatām ||
english: The ādhyaḥ cast down headlong — I lodge them within you. Let them attend upon you, goading you, rousing you without cease.

sanskrit: etās ta ādhyaḥ pra hiṇomi brahmaṇā tṛprā aśrīpurogavāḥ | tās tvā tṛṇam iva śoṣayān atho tvā rodayān bahu ||
english: These ādhyaḥ I send forth against you with the sacred formula — sated ones, with ill-fortune as their foremost cow. Let them wither you like a blade of grass, and let them make you weep bitterly.

sanskrit: ajo hy agner ajaniṣṭa śokāt so 'paśyaj janitāram agre | tena devā devatām agra āyan tena rohān arohann upa medhīyāṃsaḥ ||
english: The aja (goat; the unborn) was indeed born from Agni's grief; it beheld its progenitor at the first. By means of it the gods attained divinity in the beginning; by means of it the wise ones mounted upward upon the rungs.

sanskrit: kramadhvam agnibhir nākam ukhyāṃ hasteṣu bibhrataḥ | divas pṛṣṭhaṃ svar gatvā miśrā devebhir ādhvam ||
english: Step upward by means of the fires toward the vault of heaven, holding the cooking-pot in your hands. Having gone to the back of the sky, to the solar light, mingle and ascend together with the gods.

sanskrit: agne prehi prathamo devayatāṃ cakṣur devānām uta martyānām | iyakṣamāṇā bhṛgubhiḥ sajoṣasaḥ svar yantu yajamānāḥ svasti ||
english: O Agni, go forth first among those who seek the gods — eye of the gods and of mortals alike. May the sacrificers, striving and in fellowship with the Bhṛgus, go to the solar world in well-being.

sanskrit: svar yanto nāpekṣanta ā dyāṃ rohantu rādhasaḥ | yajñaṃ ye viśvatodhāraṃ suvidvāṃso vi tenire ||
english: Going to the solar light, they looked back no longer; let the generous ones ascend the sky. Those who, knowing well, stretched out the sacrifice that pours forth on every side.

sanskrit: odanam anajmi śavasā ghṛtena divyaṃ samudraṃ payasaṃ bṛhantam | tena geṣma sukṛtasya lokaṃ saroruhāṇā adhi nākam uttamam ||
english: I anoint the rice-porridge with strength and ghee — the divine ocean, the great milky expanse. By means of it may we reach the world of the well-doer, rising upward to the highest vault of heaven.

sanskrit: yau te pakṣāv ajarau patatriṇau yābhyāṃ rakṣāṃsy apahaṃsy odana | tābhyāṃ patyāsma sukṛtasya lokaṃ yatra rṣayaḥ prathamajāḥ purāṇāḥ ||
english: Your two ageless, winged pinions, O Odana, with which you drive away the demons — by means of those two may we fly to the world of the well-doer, where the ancient seers, the first-born of old, dwell.

sanskrit: yatas tiṣṭho divas pṛṣṭhe vyomann adhy odana | anvāyan satyadharmāṇo brāhmaṇā rādhasā saha ||
english: From where you stand, O Odana, on the back of heaven, in the wide expanse above — the Brāhmaṇas who hold the eternal law followed you along together with their generous bounty.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhāt pṛthivyā aham antarikṣam āruham antarikṣād divam āruham | divo nākasya pṛṣṭhāt svar jyotir agām aham ||
english: From the surface of the earth I have ascended to the mid-region; from the mid-region I have ascended to the sky. From the back of the sky's vault I have gone to the solar light.

sanskrit: ajo 'sy aja svargo 'si tvayā lokam aṅgirasaḥ pra jānan | taṃ lokam anu pra jñeṣma ||
english: You are the aja (unborn/goat), O aja; you are heaven. By means of you the Aṅgirasas came to know the world. That world may we come to know in turn.

sanskrit: yenā sahasraṃ vahasi yena vā sarvavedasam | tenemaṃ yajñaṃ no vaha svar deveṣu gantave ||
english: By that with which you carry a thousand, or by that with which you carry all-wealth — by that carry this sacrifice of ours to the solar world, for us to go among the gods.

sanskrit: ajaṃ ca pacata pañca caudanān | ajaṃ pañcaudanaṃ paktvā devā lokān sam ānaśuḥ ||
english: Cook the aja and the five rice-porridges. Having cooked the aja and the five rice-porridges, the gods fully attained the worlds.

sanskrit: yā te prajāpihitā purābhūd dhruveṇāśvināpa taṃ bharāmi | agniṣ ṭe tāmādyamaḥ punar dād vaiśvānaraḥ paramasmād vyomnaḥ ||
english: The offspring-channel of yours that was stopped up of old by the Aśvins through the Dhruva (fixed peg) — that I now bring back for you. May Agni Vaiśvānara give it back to you again from the highest firmament.

sanskrit: tvaṃ patiḥ śivo 'gne dvitīyo *'syai prajāṃ jaradaṣṭiṃ sṛjasva | muñcaināṃ grāhyā nirṛtir yad bandha- -agne prajāṃ prajākāmāyai dhehi ||
english: You, O Agni, are her second auspicious husband — bestow upon her progeny reaching to old age. Release her from whatever bondage Nirṛti has seized her with. O Agni, grant offspring to this woman who desires offspring.

sanskrit: tvām agne vṛṣabhaṃ vāśiteyam ācyā jānu putrakāmā saparyati | tām ā roha sumanasyamānaḥ prajāpateḥ prajayā saṃ sṛjainām ||
english: This woman who desires sons venerates you, O Agni the bull, with bent knee — she calls out to you. Mount her with benevolence; unite her with the progeny of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: tubhyaṃ nārī putrakāmeyam agne śuddhaṃ pūtaṃ ghṛtam ā juhoti | tām adhi skanda vīrayasva retodhā ugraḥ prajayā saṃ sṛjainam ||
english: For you, O Agni, this woman who desires sons pours an oblation of pure, clarified ghee. Leap upon her, exert your virility; you who hold the seed, O mighty one — unite her with progeny.

sanskrit: parvatād divo yoner gātrādgātrāt samāśṛtam | reto devasyadevasya tsarau parṇam ivādhām ||
english: From the mountain, from the womb of heaven, drawn together limb by limb — the seed of the god of gods I have placed in the womb like a leaf upon a branch.

sanskrit: indrasya jātasya pra papāta nābhis tām eko devaḥ prati jagrāha kāmī | tvayā vayaṃ brāhmaṇāḥ somapāḥ sūpayāma uta yā na sūte ||
english: The navel-cord fell at the birth of Indra; one god, the eager one, caught hold of it. By means of you, O Agni, may we Brāhmaṇas who drink Soma prosper, and also she who does not give birth.
